title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Enhancements, and Robustness Frontiers
contribution: A comprehensive survey of RAG architectures (retriever-, generator-, hybrid-, robustness-centric), enhancements, evaluation benchmarks, and open challenges, with comparative performance tables.

title: RAGTruth: A Hallucination Corpus for Developing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
contribution: Introduces RAGTruth, a ~18K-response word-level hallucination annotation corpus across QA, data-to-text, and summarization for RAG, and benchmarks detection methods including a fine-tuned Llama-2-13B detector.

title: Over-Searching in Search-Augmented Large Language Models
contribution: Introduces the over-searching phenomenon in search-augmented LLMs, proposes a Tokens-Per-Correctness metric and the OverSearchQA benchmark, and analyzes how search degrades abstention on unanswerable queries across models, retrieval quality, and multi-turn settings.

title: Why Uncertainty Estimation Methods Fall Short in RAG: An Axiomatic Analysis
contribution: Proposes an axiomatic framework with five constraints to evaluate uncertainty estimation methods in RAG, shows existing UE methods fail key axioms when context is added, and introduces a calibration function that improves AUROC and axiom satisfaction.

title: TrustRAG: Enhancing Robustness and Trustworthiness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
contribution: TrustRAG is a two-stage defense framework for RAG against corpus poisoning attacks, using K-means clustering plus ROUGE to filter malicious documents, then leveraging the LLM's internal knowledge for conflict resolution and self-assessment.

title: ReliabilityRAG: Effective and Provably Robust Defense for RAG-based Web-Search
contribution: ReliabilityRAG proposes a provably robust defense against retrieval corruption (corpus poisoning, prompt injection) in RAG by selecting a maximum independent set on an NLI-derived contradiction graph among retrieved documents, with a rank/reliability-aware tie-breaking and a weighted sample-and-aggregate framework for scalability.

title: PoisonArena: Uncovering Competing Poisoning Attacks in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
contribution: Introduces PoisonArena, a benchmark using the Bradley-Terry model to evaluate retrieval poisoning attacks on RAG under realistic multi-attacker competition, showing that strong single-attacker methods often fail under competing adversaries.

title: ADMIT: Few-shot Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on RAG-based Fact Checking
contribution: Proposes ADMIT, a few-shot, black-box knowledge poisoning attack against RAG-based fact-checking that injects semantically plausible adversarial passages to flip verdicts and produce deceptive justifications, even when authentic counter-evidence is retrieved.

title: Divide-Then-Align: Honest Alignment based on the Knowledge Boundary of RAG
contribution: Proposes Divide-Then-Align (DTA), which partitions RAG queries into four knowledge quadrants based on parametric and retrieval knowledge boundaries, then uses DPO to train the model to abstain ('I don't know') when queries fall outside both boundaries, while preserving answer accuracy.

title: The Synthetic Web: Adversarially-Curated Mini-Internets for Diagnosing Epistemic Weaknesses of Language Agents
contribution: Introduces Synthetic Web Benchmark, a procedurally generated mini-internet with ground-truth credibility labels, used to causally measure how a single rank-0 misinformation honeypot collapses frontier LLM agent accuracy and calibration despite access to truthful sources.

title: Architecture Matters: Comparing RAG Systems under Knowledge Base Poisoning
contribution: Empirically compares four RAG architectures (vanilla, agentic, MADAM-RAG, RLM) under N=1 knowledge base poisoning (naive and CorruptRAG-AK) on Natural Questions, showing a ~58pp ASR spread and decomposing attack success into retrieval- vs. content-stage effects, with a behavioral taxonomy for evaluation.

title: Disabling Self-Correction in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Stealthy Retriever Poisoning
contribution: Introduces DisarmRAG, a retriever-poisoning attack using contrastive-learning-based model editing plus iterative prompt co-optimization to inject stealthy malicious instructions that disable LLMs' self-correction ability in RAG, achieving >90% ASR while preserving benign retrieval.

title: Bounding Hallucinations: Information-Theoretic Guarantees for RAG Systems via Merlin-Arthur Protocols
contribution: Extends the Merlin-Arthur interactive proof protocol to RAG, training the generator against helpful and adversarial context provers to induce evidence-grounded answers, reject behavior, and information-theoretic (mutual-information) lower bounds on context-to-answer dependence.

title: SURE-RAG: Sufficiency and Uncertainty-Aware Evidence Verification for Selective Retrieval-Augmented Generation
contribution: Proposes SURE-RAG, a transparent aggregation protocol over pair-level claim-evidence verifier outputs (coverage, conflict, disagreement, retrieval uncertainty) for three-way sufficiency verification and selective answering with calibration on a controlled HotpotQA-derived benchmark.

title: Faithfulness-Aware Uncertainty Quantification for Fact-Checking the Output of Retrieval Augmented Generation
contribution: Proposes FRANQ, a faithfulness-aware uncertainty quantification method that decomposes claim factuality via faithfulness probability and condition-specific UQ, with isotonic calibration, and introduces a long-form QA dataset annotated for factuality and faithfulness.

title: One shot dominance: Knowledge poisoning attack on retrieval-augmented generation systems
contribution: Introduces AuthChain, a single-document poisoning attack against RAG that uses intent alignment, chain-of-evidence structuring, and authority signals to reliably mislead LLMs even on multi-hop queries and against RAG defenses.

title: Towards Dependable Retrieval-Augmented Generation Using Factual Confidence Prediction
contribution: Proposes a two-stage dependable RAG pipeline using conformal prediction to certify retrieved chunks and an attention-based (lookback-ratio) factuality classifier to detect hallucinated answers.

title: MTRAG-UN: A Benchmark for Open Challenges in Multi-Turn RAG Conversations
contribution: Introduces MTRAG-UN, a 666-task multi-turn RAG benchmark across 6 domains targeting unanswerable, underspecified, non-standalone questions and unclear/clarification responses, with retrieval and generation baselines showing models struggle with abstention and clarification.

title: Generating Leakage-Free Benchmarks for Robust RAG Evaluation
contribution: Introduces SeedRG, a semi-synthetic pipeline that uses reasoning-graph extraction and type-constrained entity replacement to generate RAG benchmarks free of parametric knowledge leakage, enabling more discriminative evaluation of RAG systems.

title: Decide Then Retrieve: A Training-Free Framework with Uncertainty-Guided Triggering and Dual-Path Retrieval
contribution: Proposes DTR, a training-free RAG framework that uses generation uncertainty (normalized negative log-likelihood) to decide whether to retrieve, plus a dual-path retrieval mechanism over query and pseudo-context with adaptive selection, improving QA accuracy while reducing unnecessary retrievals.

title: CODE: A Contradiction-Based Deliberation Extension Framework for Overthinking Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
contribution: Proposes CODE, a multi-agent framework that poisons the RAG knowledge base with contradiction-laden passages to trigger overthinking in reasoning LLMs, inflating reasoning token usage 5-25x without degrading answer accuracy.

title: PRGB Benchmark: A Robust Placeholder-Assisted Algorithm for Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation
contribution: Introduces PRGB, a placeholder-based benchmark to evaluate LLMs in RAG across multi-level noise filtering, combination, and reference reasoning, decoupling parametric knowledge via placeholder substitution.

title: NeuroGenPoisoning: Neuron-Guided Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation of LLM via Genetic Optimization of External Knowledge
contribution: Proposes NeuroGenPoisoning, a neuron-attribution-guided genetic optimization framework that crafts adversarial external passages to override an LLM's parametric memory in RAG, explicitly addressing knowledge-conflict scenarios where internal memory resists poisoning.

title: How to make Medical AI Systems safer? Simulating Vulnerabilities, and Threats in Multimodal Medical RAG System
contribution: Proposes MedThreatRAG, a multimodal poisoning attack framework (textual, visual, and cross-modal conflict injection) targeting medical RAG pipelines, and evaluates degradation on IU-Xray and MIMIC-CXR with LLaVA-Med and Qwen-VL.

title: Parenting: Optimizing Knowledge Selection of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models with Parameter Decoupling and Tailored Tuning
contribution: Proposes Parenting, which mines key parameters and decouples adherence vs. robustness subspaces in LLMs, applying tailored fine-tuning to balance following retrieved evidence vs. resisting noisy/conflicting context in RAG.

title: Enhancing Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models with In-Context Learning
contribution: Proposes in-context learning with MRC-based 'cases' (QA and conflict demonstrations) to make frozen RALMs more robust to unanswerable queries and inter-context conflicts on NQ and WebQ without fine-tuning.

title: Trustworthiness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems: A Survey
contribution: A survey defining trustworthiness in RAG across six dimensions (factuality, robustness, fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy), reviewing literature, and introducing the TRC Bench benchmark evaluating 19 LLMs.
